entries.text: Thank you for calling VeloFit. Your call may be recorded for quality assurance. Please hold for the next available agent.
Thank you for holding. My name is Sarah. How can I help you today?
Yeah, I want to return something. This is ridiculous. I bought a pair of your so-called 'performance' cycling shoes and they're complete garbage!
I'm very sorry to hear you're not happy with your purchase. I can certainly look into that for you. Do you have your order number handy?
Order number? I don't know! It's under the name Mark Peterson. Just find it! I spent a lot of money and all I got were blisters on my feet. I can't even ride!
I understand your frustration, Mr. Peterson. Let me pull up your account. One moment... Okay, I see your recent order for the Apex cycling shoes, delivered about 30 days ago. Is that correct?

Yes! And I want a refund. I'm not paying for products that injure me. The cleats seem fine, but the shoe itself is a torture device. I'm about to post reviews on every single website about this. Get me your manager!

Sir, there's no need to speak with a manager, I can absolutely handle this for you. Our standard return policy is 90 days from the date of delivery. Since you're well within that timeframe, I can process this return for a full refund right now.
Wait, really? You'll just take them back? No questions asked?

That's correct. I am sending a prepaid return label to the email address on file. Just package the cycling shoes back in their box, attach the label, and drop it off at any post office. Once our warehouse scans it in, your refund will be issued.
Oh. Well... okay then. That's... surprisingly easy. So I'll get the full amount back?
Yes, a full refund to your original payment method. The email should be in your inbox now.
Huh. I see it. Alright. Well, thank you, Sarah. I appreciate you taking care of that so quickly.
You're very welcome, Mr. Peterson. Is there anything else I can assist you with today?
Thank you for calling VeloFit. Have a good rest of your day.
